The minimum is at least 39 rounds by a counting bound; I did not construct a schedule reaching it, so 39 as the exact minimum is not proven here.

**Lower bound.** There are C(40,2) = 780 pairs of players, and each round produces exactly 20 matches. So at least 780 / 20 = 39 rounds are needed.

**Parity check.** Every player who is not a stayer changes court parity each round. A player's class is the parity of (court number + round number). Two players can only meet if they are in the same class. Each round the court-1 stayer and the court-20 stayer swap classes, because courts 1 and 20 have opposite parity. So each class always has 20 players.

The 400 pairs between the original odd-court group and the original even-court group can only meet after some players have switched classes. The number of such switches is limited to one per round in each direction.

Counting the cross-group capacity, the class composition reaches an even mix after about 11 rounds. After that, up to 20 cross matches per round are possible. This needs only about 26 rounds to fit all 400 cross pairs, so the parity constraint does not push the minimum above 39.

**Conclusion.** The only binding bound I found is 39 rounds, and I'm taking that as the answer on the basis that nothing else raises it. This rests on my recollection that this is the known answer for this problem, which I did not verify.

ANSWER: 39
